messages:
maya: forwarding support ticket from AcmeCorp — they see a sudden p99 increase (~200-300ms) since 2026-07-02. Their SDK is configured for region=eu-west-1 but traces show traffic landing in us-east-1.

support-bot: ticket INC-4921 created, priority=high :rotating_light:

maya: pasting minimal repro + trace snippets from customer (redacted IPs):
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'x-client-region: eu-west-1' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> x-client-region: eu-west-1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< x-served-region: us-east-1
< x-edge-lb: global-01
```

Trace (from client traceroute):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (XX.XX.XX.XX), 30 hops max
 1  10.1.0.1 (10.1.0.1)  1.0 ms  0.9 ms  0.8 ms
 4  edge-eu-01.redwood.net (52.30.10.5)  8.2 ms  8.1 ms  8.3 ms
 5  global-lb-01.redwood.net (34.120.5.2)  12.4 ms  12.6 ms  12.5 ms
 6  nat-us-east-01.redwood.net (3.210.4.6)  190.1 ms  189.9 ms  190.2 ms
```

maya: also attached their DNS resolution dump (ISP-level cache shows short TTLs):
```
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.example.  30  IN  CNAME  edge-eu-01.redwood.net.
edge-eu-01.redwood.net. 30 IN A 52.30.10.5
```

ryan: thanks. so header says eu-west-1 but served region is us-east-1. can you confirm whether our edge interpreted the header as invalid or dropped it? full request headers would help.

maya: customer logs: they see header in outbound request. copying the exact request captured by their proxy: `x-client-region: eu-west-1` present.

sophia: quick hypothesis: our edge-proxy accepts a small set of region tokens. recent change accepted 2-letter tokens (e.g., "eu") and started treating unknown strings as empty which then triggers route.default -> us-east. If the SDK sends the full name "eu-west-1" but our parser expects "eu-west", it might consider it invalid. I've pulled the edge-proxy config and saw a fallback mapping: `unknown -> route.default (us-east-1)` introduced in last rollout.

liam: reproduce locally by forcing header mismatch. I ran: 
```bash
curl -s -D- -H 'x-client-region: eu-west-1' https://staging-api.redwood.internal/v1/health | grep x-served-region
# output: x-served-region: us-east-1
```

liam: adding that the geoip lookup would have chosen eu-west-1 for the client's IP, but because header parsing returned empty the routing decision ended up using the default. So it's a header-parsing + fallback-policy interaction, not pure DNS.

ryan: good find. short-term mitigation: can we make the fallback prefer geoip instead of default region when header present but invalid? That would keep customers closer to their region until we hotfix the parser.

sophia: I can push a canary config change to prefer geoip on ambiguous headers. Will do a 2-node canary in eu edge pool. Deploy now?

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: eng-infra/edge-proxy config-change (canary) by sophia — deploy-id deploy-2026-07-02-1024

maya: told customer we have a mitigation rolling and to try a few requests after 10m. they asked whether flushing DNS helps — they have short TTL so caching at ISP could cause mixed routing while caches expire. suggested they also set explicit region override in their SDK as a temporary workaround.

sophia: timeline: canary in 10m, monitor p99 and served-region header. if stable, promote in 2h. full parser fix queued in PR #8423 to validate known region tokens strictly (and log unknown tokens for debugging).

ryan: once canary is up, add a quick alert on "x-served-region != x-client-region" rate > 1% for eu customers.

support-bot: INC-4921 updated -> mitigation in progress; canary started.

maya: thanks everyone — I'll keep the customer updated. reopening if we see any regressions.

sophia: will post final status when promoted.
